description:
FILED s515a (Opus, 2026-10-11) from Fable's review probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s513/review/p515a/iso-dup2.pl.  PRE-EXISTING (base and tree alike).
`open(my $f, ">&=", 1) or die; close $f; print "x\n";` -- perl keeps descriptor 1 open (an fdopen's close does not take the shared fd while STDOUT still holds it -- PerlIO refcounts the fd); PCL closes fd 1 and the program dies "Unable to flush stdout: Bad file descriptor".  #3185's %p-fdopen-alias covers the HANDLE forms (`>&=STDOUT`, `>&=`, $fh): the numeric form builds a fresh fd-stream on the SAME descriptor (%p-open-dup, `new-fd = src-fd` under eq-form), whose close closes the fd.  Fix direction: a numeric fdopen of a descriptor that a live handle already owns gets the alias of that handle's stream (or a stream whose close does not close the fd) -- probe `<&=0` and a non-standard fd too.
subject: open(my $f, '>&=', 1); close $f closes descriptor 1 -- perl keeps it (the numeric fdopen form; the handle forms are #3185's alias)
